gap: No result ChatGPT got states that EcoFlow sells a $49 Portable Power Station Grounding Adapter that EcoFlow says lets a DELTA 3 Classic, DELTA 3 Max, DELTA 2, DELTA 2 Max or DELTA Pro charge an EV. A DELTA 3 Max (2,048 Wh, $879 on 2026-11-17) plus that adapter costs $928, the cheapest maker-approved 2 kWh EV setup we could price. EcoFlow's $99 EV X-Stream adapter, by contrast, charges the power station from an EV charger and does not charge the car.
standout_why: We compared against the Jackery FAQ (cited) and ryzzun (cited). The Jackery FAQ names only the HomePower 3600 Pro Max and Explorer 5000 Plus as working with its Grounding Adapter, with no prices. Ryzzun names the Anker F3800, the Jackery models, the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max (its author's unit, with no grounding accessory mentioned) and the DELTA Pro Ultra, also with no prices. It says Tom's Guide saw a Geneverse and a BLUETTI AC200P fail to charge a Kia EV9. Neither page names EcoFlow's grounding adapter or its list of compatible models, and neither prices any setup. ChatGPT showed no product cards. We could not read wattcrate (bad SSL certificate), so it may cover part of this.
decides: A setup the maker approves for EV charging is what makes it work in an emergency. The cheapest one we found is the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max plus the $49 adapter: $928 for about 5 car miles at our page's 3.5 mi/kWh. The Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus plus its $49 adapter costs $3,548 for about 12 miles. Our BLUETTI and ALLPOWERS rows lose on this point: neither maker's store sells an EV grounding accessory, and BLUETTI's only advice is forum posts about a bonding plug. Our current page is also wrong to list the DELTA Pro 3 with the '$99 EV X-Stream adapter' as Level 2 EV charging. That adapter feeds power into the station from a J1772 charger. The DELTA Pro 3 also isn't on the grounding adapter's model list.
